summary.intent: Take part in the Lio 'Keep the Line Running' hackathon challenge: analyze Soony's confidential launch data, find where the plan hides a Collector's Edition shortfall, and build a product (now called Lighthouse) that rechecks the plan on every portal drop and acts on it, with a UI suited to procurement roles.
summary.outcome: Found the hidden gaps (art book overbooking, failed statue lot, game card offload, sleeve revision conflict, false magnet alarm) and built a polling, versioned, agent-based pipeline with approver and buyer UI. Many commits sit on `main`, with a case-flow branch and a parked chat branch. As of the last turn the hand-in at 12:00 was close and some work was not yet pushed or restarted live.

repo: Confidential portal data lives in the gitignored `data/` folder; `.env` is gitignored and `.env.example` is committed. Neither should carry real values into code or commits.

The portal API has only three endpoints (`GET /api/v1/files`, `/files/{path}`, `/archive.zip`) and no webhooks. Files change without notice and are replaced under the same name, so change detection must compare SHA-256 checksums by polling.
The team workflow is in `CLAUDE.md` and `PROGRESS.md`. Tasks are claimed with a 'Now' line in `PROGRESS.md`, and Entire hooks checkpoint on commit and push.

Main already runs an escalation loop and a phone bridge (`card_alerts.py`). The `new-approach` branch's second escalation loop and `pulse-console` app would duplicate them and bypass the duplicate-send guard and record-only mode.

The routine editor only accepts steps the trigger kind supports: 'Chase once if no answer' needs a watcher on waiting messages, 'Ask for a status' needs a watcher on shipments, and the server rejects them on 'open decisions'. The Add step menu now greys these out with the reason.
The API does not load `.env` on import, so settings such as the buyer title must be read through a helper that loads `.env` first, or they are missing after a restart.
The case flow reuses the routine diagram's connector and node components, exported from `FlowGraph.tsx`, so the two views share drawing code and cannot drift apart.
The web build is served by live and demo directly after a rebuild, but new backend endpoints need a server restart. The suite has 360 tests, and ESLint is not configured in the web app.
The role title for the approver comes from the data ('Head of Procurement'); the data has no buyer title, so it is set through a buyer title setting.

code.finding: New 'How we got here' component showing a case's agent steps (Portal, Reader, Verifier, Prediction, Approval rule, Decision, Then). It is built only from the case's own data and omits steps the data lacks. It now runs as a single top-to-bottom column because Pulse's two-per-row snake read right-to-left and confused users.

Pulse-style 'Describe it' chat on branch `jonas/pulse-ui`, backed by `POST /api/routines/describe`. It was merged then reverted because it duplicated the per-routine 'change in your words' box, clashed in colour and ignored predictions. It stays parked.

workflow: Check what a repo already does before adding features. The 'Covered' green line and the Describe chat both duplicated existing UI and were dropped or reverted.

Use separate git worktree folders per branch (`../ask-soony-pulse`, `../ask-soony-flow`) with preview servers on a copy of demo state (background off, email record-only) so live data is never touched.
Verify UI changes with headless-browser screenshots at desktop and phone size before committing.
Interviews with Soony staff should drive design. Sophia preferred the decision view over a chat pipeline, and Maren wanted decisions first, which exposed the chat misreading.
Keep untrusted or confidential material local. Findings notes and extracted data stay in gitignored `data/`, and credentials seen in chat are left out of shared docs.
Rebase onto origin before pushing when teammates have pushed, then re-run tests and the build.

friction: Misread the team's liking for Pulse and built a chat that duplicated existing UI, which cost a merge and a revert.
The first role change replaced names with roles, which the user did not want, and it made Maren's button read 'Ask Maren to approve' for her own cases.
The first two-column case flow ran right to left and confused readers.
Adding 'Chase once if no answer' looked broken because the step menu offered it on every routine, while the server rejected it on decision routines.
The first 'Fixed today' version read supplier reply fields and wrongly listed Boise's cards as a win.
Several results were not verified in a real browser: the Describe chat, the History link and the demo load.
The Routines page becomes a long wall when many routines exist.
The user interrupted several tool runs when direction needed correcting.
open_items: Push `main` (about 7 commits ahead of origin) and restart live so the sign-in choice, Maren's 'Waiting for your OK' and the heartbeat show there.
Merge `jonas/case-flow` (`4000003`) into `main` if wanted; `jonas/pulse-ui` stays parked.
Port Lucas's 'read new documents before verifying' step into `runner.run_pipeline`, keeping the skip-without-model path and the try/except, after the hand-in.
Redesign Routines as a compact list with a ⋯ menu and a duplicate-routine warning.
Support 'send email, then chase once if no answer' on decision routines through a reply-watching follow-up.
Prepare the pitch deck and video for the 12:00 hand-in.
Decide on the logo (offered a beam variant) and the Karton Nowak art book order, plus other supplier emails sent from a registered sender.
